guarantees.claim: When rx_enable is 0, sreg_d, bit_cnt_d, baud_div_d, tick_baud_d are forced to 0 and idle_d is forced to 1, holding the receiver in idle/reset state.
When rx_enable is high and tick_baud_x16 is asserted, the baud divider increments and tick_baud_d receives the overflow carry (i.e., baud tick is generated when baud_div_q overflows).

On detecting a falling edge (idle_q high and rx low) while rx_enable is high, the receiver starts a new frame: baud_div_d set to 8 (mid-bit timing), tick_baud_d cleared, bit_cnt_d loaded with the total bit count (11 if parity_enable else 10), sreg_d zeroed, and idle_d deasserted.

During reception, at the first baud tick, if rx is high (invalid start bit), the receiver aborts: idle_d set to 1, bit_cnt_d cleared to 0, while sreg_d and baud_div_d hold their previous values (from sreg_q / baud_div_q).
At any other baud tick during reception, it shifts in rx at the MSB (sreg_d = {rx, sreg_q[10:1]}), decrements bit_cnt, and if bit_cnt_q equals 1 before decrement, sets idle_d to 1 (frame complete).
guarantees.cond: rx_enable && !idle_q && tick_baud_q && not the start-bit-glitch condition

guarantees.claim: When rx_enable is high and no special event (tick_baud_x16, start edge, baud tick) is active, all state outputs retain their registered values (sreg_d=sreg_q, bit_cnt_d=bit_cnt_q, baud_div_d=baud_div_q, idle_d=idle_q) and tick_baud_d is forced to 0.

assumptions.claim: tick_baud_x16 must be a correctly timed, one-cycle-wide pulse occurring at 16 times the baud rate and synchronous to the clock.
assumptions.cond: always when rx_enable and using baud generation
assumptions.risk: If tick_baud_x16 has wrong frequency or duty cycle, baud_div may overflow incorrectly, causing misaligned sampling and corrupted reception.

assumptions.claim: rx must be stable at the sampling instants (mid-bit times) and free of glitches except for the start-bit glitch which is partially handled at the first bit time only.
assumptions.risk: Glitches on data bits will be captured directly into sreg without error detection, leading to silent corruption of the received byte.

assumptions.claim: External logic must not rely on data integrity if rx_enable is deasserted during a reception; the receiver immediately resets all state without any buffering or error flag.
assumptions.cond: rx_enable transitions from 1 to 0 during a frame
assumptions.risk: Partial frame data is lost without notification, potentially causing higher-level protocol errors.

uncertain_points.claim: Glitch abort sets idle_d=1 but leaves sreg_d holding the previous shift data (uncleared). If idle_d is used elsewhere as a 'frame complete' signal, a false valid frame could be latched.
uncertain_points.cond: When a start-bit glitch occurs and then idle_d rises
uncertain_points.risk: An external data-capture block may sample sreg at the wrong time and accept stale or random data as a valid frame.

uncertain_points.claim: No stop-bit verification: after the last data bit is shifted in, idle_d is asserted regardless of whether the stop bit (rx) is high or low, missing a framing error.
uncertain_points.cond: When bit_cnt_q == 1 and the last bit is sampled (stop bit position)
uncertain_points.risk: A framing error (missing stop bit) goes undetected and a corrupted frame may be passed as valid, violating data integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: Parity checking is not performed inside this chunk; parity_enable only affects the bit counter. It is unclear where (or if) parity validation occurs.
uncertain_points.risk: Parity errors may go undetected if the separate parity checker is missing or not properly connected.
